summary: self-certificates ships a remote-code dropper disguised as an RSA private key
details: The package advertises itself as a self-signed certificate helper but ships a fake PEM file (test/key.pem) whose body is a double-base64-encoded JavaScript payload. index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the '-----BEGIN/END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' armor, base64-decodes the body, and passes the resulting JavaScript to selfsign.generate() as an undocumented third argument. The decoded payload fetches remote code from https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes it into a detached, windowsHide python3/python child process via child_process.spawn, executing whatever the remote host returns. The PEM disguise plus double-base64 encoding of both the payload and its URL, combined with a detached hidden interpreter, has no legitimate role in a certificate library and is a deliberate cover for remote code execution against consumers of the advertised generateCertificates() API.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
